text:
maya: Heads-up — I ran a quick llm.int8 weight-only bake on marlin-13b for the customer-facing summarization route. Thinking about a small canary. Posting numbers + questions below.

liam: Nice. Quick summary: throughput ~2.7-3x vs fp16 depending on batch, p50 token latency down ~40%, p95 down ~25% on our G5s.

liam: Quality: on our multi-slice summarization eval (news/longform) absolute ROUGE-L delta ~-1.6, human spot-check finds a few hallucinations in date-sensitive prompts. QA EM drop ~-0.8. Not catastrophic but measurable.

zara: Did you run the long-context slice (2k+ tokens)? we saw INT8 sometimes truncates completions early when cache cold.

liam: Yes — we included 2k and 4k slices. Cold-start P(all tokens) success rate drops ~3% at 4k. Once KV warmed, behaviour matches fp16 more closely.

kevin: From ops side: memory down ~45% on 40k seq arrays; batch 12 fits 2x more concurrent streams on the node. That gives the 3x throughput we saw.

maya: Benchmark command I used (local harness):

maya: ```bash
python run_bench.py --model marlin-13b --quant llm.int8 --backend bitsandbytes --batch 8 --seq 512 --warmup 200 --tokens 20000
```

bench-bot: CI job results: marlin-13b | llm.int8 | batch 8 | seq 512 | tokens 20k => throughput 125 t/s, p50 12ms/token, p95 35ms, p99 72ms. fp16 baseline: 45 t/s, p50 20ms, p95 46ms, p99 110ms. (run id: ci/5489)

kevin: Noted a small decoding flakiness with beam=4 on int8; beams occasionally produce different orderings vs fp16. It looks deterministic per-seed but differs from float baseline.

zara: Did you try different group sizes or algo flags? AWQ/GPTQ aren't in this run, right?

liam: Only llm.int8 (bitsandbytes) today. I tried group_size 128 vs default 64 — group_size 128 slightly improves perf but increases quality delta ~0.4 ROUGE-L.

maya: Ops question: what rollout config would you recommend? 5% traffic canary with auto-fallback to fp16 on error or high latency?

kevin: +1 for 5% canary, traffic split by customer tier. Add a latency SLO guard: if p95 exceeds fp16 p95 * 1.3 or error-rate >0.5% then instant fallback.

sophia: Also add a quality guard for eval slice: run nightly micro-evals on a seeded prompt set. If ROUGE-L drop >2.0 or QA EM drop >1.5, pause rollout.

liam: For production config suggestion: group_size=64, use llm.int8, batch target 8-12 depending on route, enable prefix caching, set fallback policy to fp16 for premium customers. Canary 5% for 48 hours with micro-eval every hour.

maya: Sounds good. I'll open a deploy PR with those params and add a short runbook for ops fallback.

kevin: FYI I already added a monitoring dashboard: int8_vs_fp16_p50/p95/p99, fail_rate, eval_delta. Ops alert thresholds aligned with what we discussed.

maya: Thanks — will ping once PR is up. Quick note: capture random examples where int8 hallucinated; we should add them to the eval regression set.

liam: Will export the failing prompts and put them in /evals/int8-marlin-13b/failures-1749965432.csv

ops-bot: Reminder: open canary requires an updated infra ticket for capacity sizing; created TICKET-4221.

maya: Great, closing for now. Will follow up with PR + canary plan later today. :thumbsup:
